moment: the engine states its own budgets and its own recent history — ruling 19's surface 8, completed
source: JOS-502 (owner ruling 19: "the performance chip should incl perf of the server in end state"; the two ops surface 8 names, after 07-perf-snapshot.json shipped the third)
note: FOUR ANSWERS, AND THE FIRST TWO ARE THE ONES THE WHOLE SHAPE EXISTS FOR. (1) A LAUNCHED ENGINE'S BUDGETS: both rows present, both `unmeasured`, `measured` ABSENT on both — never a zero and never an optimistic pass, because a just-launched engine is exactly the window in which somebody opening the performance panel is most likely to be looking, and a budget that reads green there is green for the period in which it knows least. The definitions are served anyway, which is ruling 3 in one object: the ceiling and its caveat are what let a reader judge instead of trusting a colour, and the `foldRate` note is where the UNMET G3 GOAL is said out loud (52.5 s against a 20 s goal) so that a passing row can never be misread as a goal reached. (2) THE SAME BUILD LIVE, WITH ONE ROW FAILING: the fold rate cleared its floor and the serve path did not, which is what a wedged ingest looks like from the panel — and note that the serve row's own `note` still says it is a wedge detector rather than a compute budget, because the number includes the ~10 Hz coalescing beat. `limit` and `measured` are RENDERED STRINGS in one en-US vocabulary (ruling 25), not numbers with a unit the caller has to know: the two budgets are measured in different units, the comparison that produces the verdict is arithmetic, and ruling 4 puts arithmetic and rendering on this side of the wire. (3) AN EMPTY TIMELINE, which is the commonest honest answer — the ring is filled by the ingest thread's own beat, so an engine with nothing attached has sampled nothing, and `capacity` and `cadenceMs` are on the answer regardless because a client inferring the horizon from the LENGTH would infer it wrongly for the whole first period of every generation. (4) A FILLED RING, oldest first, and every figure in a moment is an INTERVAL rather than a running total: `perf.snapshot` already answers the cumulative question, and a history exists to say that this ten seconds cost four times what the last ten did. The third moment here is QUIET — zero frames, zero weight, no latency at all — and it is recorded rather than skipped, because a ring that dropped its silent samples would compress a lull into no space and make the busy moments either side of it look adjacent. `foldToFrameUsMax` absent in that moment means no frame in the window had a fold behind it, never zero microseconds.

budgets.label: fold rate
budgets.note: The floor is an eighth of the 7.8 MB/s this engine measured on the author's machine, so that a debug build or a wedged scan is what trips it rather than a busy afternoon. It is not the program's goal: folding the owner's 209 MB log in 20 s is the G3 goal and it is NOT met at this release (52.5 s, 3.8 MB/s measured). A pass here says this build is not broken, never that the goal is reached.

budgets.label: serve latency
budgets.note: Measured fold-to-outbox, so the engine's ~10 Hz coalescing beat and the tail's poll interval are inside it: 56 ms for a one-row diff is a beat, not work. The ceiling sits two orders of magnitude above anything observed and is a wedge detector rather than a performance budget. There is no compute-only serve measurement in this build.
